description: Ten control voltages laid out as the Tree of Life, each worked out from the real positions of the planets and the computer clock, plus a two-bus mixer of all ten

params.text: Sets how fast simulated time runs, from real time up to a hundred million times it, which is about three years a second at the top
Chooses whether the sky is the real one from the computer clock or the warped one the knob beside it drives
Sets the fixed voltage the Malkuth output carries, from -5V to 5V
Sets how much of that sephirah goes into that bus, from -1 to 1, negative settings subtracting it

outputs.text: Neptune's heliocentric longitude as a sine, ±5V, which drifts so slowly it is near a fixed voltage
The zodiac sign Uranus is in, as one of 12 steps of a twelfth of a volt
A square wave from Saturn's heliocentric longitude, one cycle every 30 degrees, 0V or 10V
A square wave from Jupiter's heliocentric longitude, one cycle every 30 degrees, 0V or 10V
Mars's heliocentric longitude as a sine, ±5V, its speed uneven because the orbit is eccentric
A ramp from 0V to 10V over the solar year
The geocentric position of Venus on one axis, ±5V; take it with the jack beside it into a scope to draw the eight-year Venus pentagram
The geocentric position of Venus on the other axis, ±5V; take it with the jack beside it into a scope to draw the eight-year Venus pentagram
Mercury's elongation from the sun, ±5V, which turns back on itself through each retrograde
A 1ms trigger at 10V at each real Mercury station, the moment its apparent motion reverses
The illuminated fraction of the moon, 0V at new moon and 10V at full
The fixed voltage set by the knob above it
That bus of the Da'at mixer, every sephirah scaled by its own knob and summed, clamped to ±10V

notes: nothing here needs patching in: every output is computed from orbital elements and the computer clock, with no network and no input jacks
the readout beside the time switch shows the date the sky is being drawn for, which in warp mode runs away from the present
menu: Set time to now — puts the simulated date back to the present moment

outputs.1: 1V per octave · stepped · one channel only
